subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw own for exec-backed external secrets under supervised gateway restarts?
rationale: Changing fail-fast startup behavior can either reduce provider rate-limit amplification or weaken credential fail-closed guarantees, and adding retry/config/circuit-breaker behavior changes a security-sensitive startup contract.

options.title: Generic guarded startup policy
options.body: Add a core-owned bounded startup retry/degrade/cooldown strategy with operator-visible diagnostics and focused live proof, while leaving backend batching and caching to resolver plugins.

options.title: Configurable retry policy
options.body: Add `secrets.retryPolicy` or per-provider retry knobs, accepting the additional config, docs, migration, and upgrade-review surface.

options.title: Keep fail-fast plus docs
options.body: Keep current fail-fast semantics and document launchd/systemd restart limits plus external caching resolver plugins as the supported mitigation.

recommendation.title: Generic guarded startup policy
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned bounded startup retry/degrade/cooldown strategy with operator-visible diagnostics and focused live proof, while leaving backend batching and caching to resolver plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail ties joshavant most directly to the external secrets runtime and eager gateway activation design that this policy would change.
